troll.d: In online chat or multiplayer games, a person who deliberately provokes or annoys others to get a reaction. The word also has older folklore meanings; context matters.
In folklore, a supernatural being, often described as a giant or creature living in caves or mountains.

trolling.d: Posting or saying provocative things to bait a reaction. In a game, the same word can also mean playful joking, so ask what the speaker intends before treating it as hostile.

griefing.d: In multiplayer games, deliberately disrupting other players, such as damaging their builds or repeatedly interfering with play. This describes behavior, not proof of someone's intent.

goofing.d: Playing around or acting silly rather than making a serious request.

survival.d: Minecraft game mode where a player normally has health, hunger, and resource limits. The bot verifies its own server-reported mode before autonomous work.

creative.d: Minecraft game mode with building-focused abilities. The bot does not grant itself Creative; any mode change must be explicitly requested and authorized by the server.

redstone.d: Minecraft material and system used to transmit signals and build mechanisms; the name also refers to redstone dust, ore, blocks, and related components.

ore.d: A naturally occurring Minecraft block that can contain a resource, such as coal, iron, copper, gold, redstone, lapis lazuli, diamond, or emerald.

strip mining.d: A planned mining pattern using parallel tunnels or lanes. Before any automation, confirm the target, depth, tunnel length, spacing, and safe return path; this app does not yet implement a verified multi-lane strip-mining plan.
